sentences.text: Aggrieved by the order passed in W.P.No.103464/2018 by the learned Single Judge, the present writ appeal is filed by the second respondent therein.
2. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per the status in the writ petition.
3. The land of the petitioner was acquired by the second respondent for widening of the existing Hubballi- Dharwad road.
A Price Fixation Committee was constituted which fixed the amount payable for the land losers and called upon them to come and receive the compensation under the consent award.
Similarly, notice was also sent to the petitioner to sign the consent award and receive the compensation accordingly.

However, as there was a dispute with regard to title of the property pending before the Civil Court, petitioner was unable to execute necessary documents in favour of second NC: 2024:KHC-D:5195-DB respondent consenting for the acquisition and receiving the compensation.
4. The land concerned was acquired for the public purpose and road construction on the said land commenced.
As the petitioner did not accept the consent award, the second respondent was constrained to pass a general award as per Section 28 of the Karnataka Highways Act, 1964 (for short, 'the Act').

Subsequently, the petitioner, in O.S.No.137/2013 obtained an order from the Civil Court on an Interlocutory Application filed by him in the said original suit, wherein the Civil Court directed the second respondent in the writ petition to pay the compensation in respect of the land acquired in favour of the petitioner and the petitioner received the said compensation under protest.

The following order was passed by the Civil Court:
ORDER "I.A No.5 filed by the applicant/plaintiffs U/Sec.151 of CPC is hereby rejected.
I.A. No.4 filed by the applicant/defendant No.2 is hereby allowed.

Fifteen Lakhs, Fifty-Eight Thousand and Three Hundred and Ninety Three only)
through an account payee cheque to the defendant No.2 on proper identification and against passing of vouchers, under intimation to this court subject to following The Special Land Acquisition Officer vs Shri. 2 conditions:
1) The defendant No.2 shall execute an indemnity bond in favour of the State of Karnataka for above said amount or as per rules to be directed by said office.
2) He shall redeposit said amount with interest in accordance with law, if order of this court or of our Hon'ble High Court is set aside by any Hon'ble Appellate Courts or if the claim of defendant No.2 is set aside by any proper authority.
Issue direction accordingly.
No order as to costs."
5. The case of the petitioner is that, he is the owner of the property concerned and the said land was acquired by the second respondent.

However, as the brother of his vendor has raised a dispute and O.S.No.137/2013 was filed in this regard, he was not in a position to accept the compensation under the Consent Award though he was agreeable for the same and he was in fact constrained to obtain an order from the Civil Court by filing necessary Interlocutory Application in O.S.No.137/2013 to receive the compensation and that NC: 2024:KHC-D:5195-DB the said suit having been disposed of in his favour, he alone is entitled to receive compensation for acquisition of the land concerned and that the said fact has not been disputed by the respondents.

It is further submitted that the petitioner is entitled to receive best possible compensation that is payable to him and hence, he intended to opt for Consent Award and for that reason, preferred W.P.No.103464/2018.

6. Learned Single Judge has allowed the writ petition filed by the petitioner and has directed the authorities concerned to consider the representation of the petitioner to pay him as per the consent award.
Aggrieved by the same, the present writ appeal is filed.
7. The case of the second respondent is that, there has been no dereliction of duty on the part of the second respondent.

It has acquired the land concerned in accordance with law and a General Award has also been passed in accordance with law and as per the directions of the Civil Court compensation is determined, under which NC: 2024:KHC-D:5195-DB the compensation has been paid to the petitioner.

It is further submitted that the second respondent initially sent a notice to the petitioner calling upon him to accept the amount by giving his consent and if he had done so within the time stipulated, petitioner would have been entitled to receive the amount.

It is also submitted that the petitioner cannot choose between the General Award and Consent Award as and when he likes and he is required to elect either the General Award or the Consent Award within the time stipulated.
It is also submitted that the action of the petitioner amounts to approbating and reprobating at the same time.

It is also urged that the petitioner is having an alternative and efficacious remedy, in the sense, that if he is not satisfied by the award, he could always approach the Reference Court for enhancement of the same.
That he could not have filed writ petition praying for payment of the amount of compensation as per the Consent Award.

It is also submitted that the petitioner would be entitled to Consent Award as per Section 27 of the Act and on failure to NC:
2024:KHC-D:5195-DB exercise that option within the time stipulated, Section 28 of the Act comes The Special Land Acquisition Officer vs Shri. Arun S/O Venkanna Navali on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176161525/
3 into play and respondents left with no other alternative other than passing the General Award and it is submitted that the statute has to be interpreted as per the literal meaning of the statute and if the same is done, then the petitioner is not entitled to the Consent Award.
8.

sentences.text: For the aforementioned reasons, it is prayed that the order passed by the learned Single Judge be set aside and writ petition be dismissed.

9. The question that arises for consideration in the instant writ appeal is:
"Whether once a General Award is passed under Section 28 of the Karnataka Highways Act, can this Court in exercise of its writ jurisdiction set aside the General Award and direct the authorities concerned to pass a Consent Award at the request of a party whose land has been acquired?"
10.

The relevant facts to decide the aforementioned question are, though the land of the petitioner has been NC: 2024:KHC-D:5195-DB acquired, he did not object to the said acquisition, second respondent asked him to give the consent for acquisition and accept the compensation as per the Price Fixation Committee, the petitioner was not in a position to accept the same as there was inter se dispute with the private person regarding ownership of the property and he has requested for payment of the award upon resolution of the dispute, which has been denied to him on the ground that the time for the same is over and a General Award had also been passed.
11. Article 300A of the Constitution of India mandates that, no person shall be deprived of his property save by the authority of law.
When land of a person is acquired by the State for public purpose, compensation has to be paid to him and the same has to be just, fair and reasonable.

When it comes to payment of compensation, the provisions of law regarding the same has to be considered as part of Social Welfare Legislation and the interpretation which is beneficial to the land loser has to NC: 2024:KHC-D:5195-DB be adopted.
The relevant statute itself prescribes as to how compensation has to be assessed.
In the instant case, Sections 27 and 28 of the Act stipulate as to determination of the amount of compensation, which are extracted below:

"27. Determination of amount of compensation by agreement.--The amount of compensation payable under section 26, the persons to whom it is to be paid and the apportionment of such amount among the persons interested therein, shall be determined by agreement between the Highway Authority or any officer authorised by the State Government and the person or persons claiming interest therein.

28. Determination of amount of compensation in default of agreement.--(1) In default of any agreement under section 27, the Highway Authority or the officer authorised by the State Government shall, subject to the provisions of this Act, after holding an enquiry, make an award determining,--
(a) the true area of the land, if any, acquired;

4 (b) the amount of compensation to be paid under Section 26;
(c) the apportionment if any, of such compensation amount among all persons known or believed to be entitled thereto.
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:5195-DB (2) In determining the amount of compensation, the matter specified in Sections 23 and 24 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as amended by the Schedule to this Act, shall be taken into consideration."
12.

sentences.text: Thus, the Highway Authority has to first assess the compensation payable under Section 26 of the Act and pass a Consent Award.
It is only in default of any agreement, under Section 27 of the Act a General Award will be passed.
The statute or the Rules made thereunder does not stipulates the time within which a person has to exercise his right for claiming the Consent Award.
Thus, it has to be within a reasonable time and the authorities are always at liberty to call upon the persons concerned to exercise their right within the stipulated time.
The same has been done in the instant case by the second respondent.

However, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, the petitioner has not been in a position to exercise the option to receive the Consent Award as there was a dispute of ownership of the property concerned.

Once the same has been resolved, he has approached the authorities to pay him the compensation - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:5195-DB as per the Consent Award and it is not the case of the respondents that petitioner is not the owner of the property.
Payment of money in favour of the petitioner as per the consent award is much more beneficial to the petitioner.

The Courts in umpteen number of instances of similar nature, at the request of the land losers, has set aside the General Award and has directed the authorities concerned to pay the compensation as per the Consent Award.
13. For the aforementioned reasons, we do not find any error in the order passed by the learned Single Judge in W.P.No.103464/2018 and the writ appeal is hereby dismissed.
